**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve paragraph spacing within loose Markdown lists**

For loose lists such as `- first\n\n- second`, CommonMark retains paragraph wrappers inside the list items, but this branch classifies every paragraph inside a list as `li` regardless of whether its paragraph token is hidden. Consequently, `markdown_px()` uses only the `li` style and gives loose lists exactly the same height as tight lists, ignoring the paragraph margins supplied by the profile. With nonzero paragraph margins, the underestimate grows with the number of items and can recommend a height that clips the list. Preserve the visible paragraph structure and its spacing, or mark loose lists as unestimated.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve margins between separate consecutive lists**

For Markdown containing adjacent lists of different types, such as `- a\n\n1. b`, the parser produces two separate lists but flattens both into consecutive `li` blocks. This condition therefore treats them as one continuous list and omits the collapsed list margin between them. With the synthetic profile in `test_layout_sizing.py`, this measures 104 px instead of 118 px, underestimating the required component height. Preserve list boundaries during parsing and apply `list_margin` between distinct lists without adding it between items of the same list.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
